title: Separable Rank of Radial Kernels in Two and Higher Dimensions: Machine-Checked Proofs in Lean 4 and Isabelle/HOL
abstract: A d-variate kernel K : X_0 x ... x X_{d-1} -> K has separable rank at most N if it is a sum of N coordinatewise products sum_{n=0}^{N-1} prod_{j=0}^{d-1} f_{n,j}(x_j). On a d-dimensional Cartesian grid of support width L, a rank-R kernel evaluates in d R L one-dimensional taps per grid point rather than L^d. While a positive Gaussian exp(-alpha ||x||^2) has separable rank 1, approximating flat-top or oscillatory isotropic kernels---such as defocus disks, Airy point-spread functions, circular low-pass filters, or band-limited wave propagators---with finite coordinatewise separable rank relies on signed or oscillatory profiles built from complex-rate Gaussians and exponential polynomials. We give a complete machine-checked characterization in Lean 4 (with Mathlib) of the d-way separable rank of continuous circularly and spherically symmetric kernels K(x) = phi(||x||^2) on R^d for all d >= 2: (1) separableRank(K) < infinity over R if and only if phi agrees on [0, infinity) with a well-formed exponential-polynomial representation sum_i Re(P_i(s) exp(lambda_i s)) (nonzero polynomials P_i, distinct rates lambda_i with Im(lambda_i) >= 0, and real coefficients when Im(lambda_i) = 0); (2) over C, a continuous radial profile psi(||x||^2) has exact d-way separable rank sum_{mu in S} ((d - 1) deg P_mu + 1) for nonzero polynomials P_mu at distinct rates; (3) over R, a continuous radial profile phi(||x||^2) has exact d-way separable rank sum_i c_d(P_i, lambda_i) where each real-rate component (Im(lambda_i) = 0) costs (d - 1) deg P_i + 1 real d-way products (achieved by real Lagrange interpolation) and each nonreal conjugate-pair component (Im(lambda_i) > 0) costs R_i = 2(d - 1) deg P_i + d real d-way products, achieved via an alternating R_i-point root-of-unity polynomial-product identity (giving d rather than 2^{d-1} real products for a complex Gaussian when deg P_i = 0) and proved optimal by Alder-Strassen degree peeling over R; and (4) in d = 2, scalar extension R -> C preserves rank unconditionally, whereas for d >= 3 it can strictly lower rank (e.g. Re(exp(i ||x||^2)) has complex rank 2 and real rank d, and ||x||^2 cos(||x||^2) in d = 3 has complex rank 6, real border rank at most 6, and exact real rank 7); moreover, in d = 2 the exact rank equals the degree of the minimal monic constant-coefficient half-line differential annihilator p(D) phi_C = 0 (p in C[X]). Necessity reduces to showing that a continuous one-parameter semigroup M : [0, infinity) -> A is an exponential M(t) = exp(t A). Alongside the 96-line Banach-algebra integral-smoothing proof used in the main development, we formalize four finite-dimensional alternatives---one by finite differences in Lean 4 and three by Euler's infinitesimal step in Lean 4 and Isabelle/HOL using a homogeneous common-scale normalization eta = eps + ||M(eps) - 1|| that avoids any a priori difference-quotient bound---and compare their lengths, library reliance, and generality. Finally, we connect the root-of-unity identity to planar harmonic ("beach-ball") differential operators and evaluate two GPU-verified numerical applications on an NVIDIA RTX 4070 Ti Super: (i) minimax 2-D circular lens blur, showing how nuclear-norm-optimal GL_N(R) rebalancing on rowSpan(K) eliminates up to 1,110x intermediate cancellation so float16 buffers stay within 0.16/255 of float64 (in contrast to d >= 3, where Kruskal's theorem forbids continuous basis rotations), and (ii) explicit 3-D acoustic wave-equation leapfrog propagators, identifying Kowalczyk and van Walstijn's 27-point IWB stencil as the single-real-Gaussian (R = 1) baseline and designing certified von Neumann-stable multi-Gaussian propagators (R = 4--9) that cut directional phase-velocity error up to 0.80 pi from 9.23%--19.71% to 0.055% (381x--529x faster wall-clock and 731x less memory than 27-point IWB at a 0.1% dispersion tolerance).
